project.title: 1957 Nash Metropolitan — Restoration in Progress
project.description:
Purchased as a remarkably solid but unfinished 1957 Nash Metropolitan, this project is being completed with a simple philosophy: preserve the character of the car, correct what matters, and invest where the finished result will have the greatest impact. This living project follows the restoration from its as-acquired condition and mechanical foundation through body preparation, interior work, electrical sorting, paint, trim, final assembly and road testing.

Paint milestone — October 2026: Following the four coats of white applied on October 10, the white sections were carefully masked and the prepared upper body and hood received their yellow color. The latest photo sequence follows the car from primer and final masking through freshly applied yellow paint to the reveal of its yellow-and-white finish. Reflections across the panels capture the gloss, while the two-tone layout brings the Metropolitan's distinctive curves back into focus.

Current status: The yellow-and-white paint is now applied, marking a major step toward the finished car. The restoration continues with paint finishing as needed, glass, lights, trim and hood-ornament installation, upholstery, final assembly and road testing. The hood ornament has already been test-fitted for alignment, and the original bench-seat frame has been sandblasted, powder coated in satin black and reassembled, ready for upholstery.

Updated October 12, 2026. Preserving Americana, one car at a time.

Purchased as a remarkably solid but unfinished 1957 Nash Metropolitan, this project is being completed with a simple philosophy: preserve the character of the car, correct what matters, and invest where the finished result will have the greatest impact. This living project follows the restoration from its as-acquired condition and mechanical foundation through body preparation, interior work, electrical sorting, paint, trim, final assembly and road testing.

Paint milestone — October 2026: Following the four coats of white applied on October 10, the white sections were carefully masked and the prepared upper body and hood received their yellow color. The latest photo sequence follows the car from primer and final masking through freshly applied yellow paint to the reveal of its yellow-and-white finish. Reflections across the panels capture the gloss, while the two-tone layout brings the Metropolitan's distinctive curves back into focus.

Current status: The yellow-and-white paint is now applied, marking a major step toward the finished car. The restoration continues with paint finishing as needed, glass, lights, trim and hood-ornament installation, upholstery, final assembly and road testing. The hood ornament has already been test-fitted for alignment, and the original bench-seat frame has been sandblasted, powder coated in satin black and reassembled, ready for upholstery.

THE VISION
This completed Nash Metropolitan, finished in the same yellow-and-white combination planned for our car, represents the visual direction for this restoration. It is shown here as inspiration only—not as the finished Fitzgerald Classics project.
The Starting Point
The Metropolitan entered the Fitzgerald Classics project as a remarkably complete little car with strong restoration potential. The goal from the outset was a high-quality driver—preserving its unmistakable character while making thoughtful improvements where they mattered most.
Interior — A Solid Foundation
The interior was documented early in the project so the restoration could preserve the Metropolitan’s simple mid-century character while identifying the areas that would benefit most from refinishing and replacement.
Rebuilt 1500cc Engine
The rebuilt 1500cc engine gave the project a valuable head start, allowing much of the restoration effort to focus on presentation, reliability and finishing work.
Establishing the Body Line
The long side character line was carefully laid out during body preparation to ensure the eventual two-tone finish follows the Metropolitan’s distinctive proportions and creates the right visual break between the yellow and white paint.
Current Status — September 2026
Bodywork is well underway, with the car stripped for correction and preparation before its planned period-inspired yellow-and-white final finish.
Test-Fitting the Side Trim
Before drilling the new trim mounting holes and committing to the final two-tone paint break, the new side trim was temporarily installed to verify fit, establish the correct mounting-hole locations, confirm that the molding aligned properly along the body, and determine exactly where the paint line should fall.

Much of this work will be hidden once the seat is finished, but it is an important part of bringing this Nash back to life.

The bodywork and paint preparation are finally finished. With the rear body carefully masked, our 1957 Nash Metropolitan is ready for the first phase of its two-color paint process. This view documents the preparation before the white was applied.

1963 Ford Galaxie 500 Convertible
A complete visual journey from a tired blue survivor to a refined white-and-turquoise American classic. This Fitzgerald Classics restoration follows the Galaxie through body preparation, paint, interior reconstruction, detail work and final assembly—preserving the character of Ford’s full-size 1960s convertible while giving every surface the attention it deserved.

project.title: 1957 Nash Metropolitan — Restoration in Progress
project.description:
Purchased as a remarkably solid but unfinished 1957 Nash Metropolitan, this project is being completed with a simple philosophy: preserve the character of the car, correct what matters, and invest where the finished result will have the greatest impact. This living project follows the restoration from its as-acquired condition and mechanical foundation through body preparation, interior work, electrical sorting, paint, trim, final assembly and road testing.

Paint milestone — October 2026: Following the four coats of white applied on October 10, the white sections were carefully masked and the prepared upper body and hood received their yellow color. The latest photo sequence follows the car from primer and final masking through freshly applied yellow paint to the reveal of its yellow-and-white finish. Reflections across the panels capture the gloss, while the two-tone layout brings the Metropolitan's distinctive curves back into focus.

Current status: The yellow-and-white paint is now applied, marking a major step toward the finished car. The restoration continues with paint finishing as needed, glass, lights, trim and hood-ornament installation, upholstery, final assembly and road testing. The hood ornament has already been test-fitted for alignment, and the original bench-seat frame has been sandblasted, powder coated in satin black and reassembled, ready for upholstery.

Updated October 12, 2026. Preserving Americana, one car at a time.
